evidence: Judge agent+model: task.toml:30-35 [verifier.env] is byte-for-byte the frozen block from staged-task-contract.md (REWARDKIT_JUDGE="claude-code", REWARDKIT_MODEL="z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx", ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL="https://openrouter.ai/api", ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}", ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=""); test.sh:63-66 refuses to grade if either is unset. All five judge.toml files carry only judge = "claude-code" fallback (line 2) with no model/reasoning_effort/temperature/weight key in [judge] (grep for model|temperature|reasoning in judge.toml: no hits). Pinned CLIs/browser: tests/Dockerfile:16-22 installs @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281, @openai/codex@0.151.0, @playwright/mcp@0.0.79, express@5.1.0, better-sqlite3@12.4.1; :31 harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7; :33-38 Chromium installed by the playwright CLI bundled inside the exact-version @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 and symlinked to /usr/local/bin/chromium, which every judge.toml passes via --executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium. tests/Dockerfile, test.sh, tools/score.py, tools/restart_mcp.py, scoring.toml and environment/Dockerfile are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff: SAME; tests/Dockerfile sha256 72998ab8...5fdd both), so shared tools are canonical. Fixed clock: no graded rule depends on the calendar/wall-clock date. Time-related grading is (a) relative order (Activity newest first, 30 most recent messages, unread 'since last opened', most recent move undo) and (b) a real-elapsed latency bound ('within fifteen seconds', instruction.md:5, hireops_rules.md:117) that is measured by waiting, not by date. No criterion grades relative times ('ago'), expiries, due dates or 'today'. Golden orders by monotonic id (index.js:158,166,189,199 ORDER BY id / position, id), and seed timestamps are fixed literals (2026-07-01..; seed_data.json), so results do not vary with run date. Hence no fixed-clock statement is required and none is missing. Network public (task.toml:37-38) is explicitly not a defect for this row. Temperature/prompt-version markers not required per client sheet. Broken-app probe: an app that shows relative timestamps or orders by created_at would still be graded on observed order within one run, never against a date, so no run-date drift. Conforming-alternative probe: an app ordering activity by wall-clock timestamp instead of id still satisfies 'newest first' within the run; nothing in grading pins the golden's id choice. Limits: transitive Playwright/Chromium build number and base-image tags (node:22-bookworm-slim, python:3.12-slim, unpinned apt) are tag-pinned, not digest-pinned; these are template-controlled and the deterministic sheet treats unpinned apt as NOTE. No configured judge run exists in the raw evidence index (its scope says full configured grading is absent), so runtime judge/Chromium versions were not observed; static pinning is what this row measures.
